# GGAAG Finance Notes

> Practical personal finance notes written with the math shown: cash flow, emergency funds, index funds, asset allocation, and scam awareness. Bilingual (English primary, Chinese toggle). All content is educational, not financial advice.

Site: https://blog.ggaag.com
Language: en (primary), zh (client-side toggle, same URLs)

## Guides

- [Start Here: The Order of Operations for Your Money](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-start): The sequence that matters — employer match, high-interest debt, emergency fund, then investing.
- [Track Your Cash Flow](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-ledger): A three-category tracking system (fixed / flexible / irregular) and the three questions to answer after 30 days.
- [The Emergency Fund](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-emergency-fund): Sizing from expenses (3-6 months), where to park it, and three failure modes.
- [Index Funds and Dollar-Cost Averaging](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-index-dca): What DCA actually earns; a 1% fee gap consumes ~23% of final wealth over 40 years.
- [Compound Interest: Two Details Nobody Mentions](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-compound): Rear-loaded gains (half the 30-year result lands in the final decade) and nominal vs real returns.
- [Asset Allocation](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-allocation): Three-bucket structure and scheduled rebalancing, with a worked 60/40 example.
- [Avalanche vs Snowball](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-debt-order): Same $600/month budget simulated on the same three debts — $923 and 2 months apart, first payoff 4 months earlier with snowball.
- [Investment Scams](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-scam): Three structures every pitch reduces to, plus a one-question test.
- [Nasdaq Drawdowns in Numbers](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-nasdaq-drawdown): Every major Nasdaq decline since 2000 — depth and time-to-recovery — and the three moves with math behind them.
- [Where to Park Cash in October 2026](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-cash-rates): FDIC averages vs top yields (0.38% vs ~4-5%), the inertia tax quantified, and CD-ladder math that wins whether the Fed hikes or cuts.
- [The Grad Job Market Broke in 2026](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-grad-jobs): Recent grads now out-unemploy the overall workforce (5.7% vs 4.4%, widest gap on record) — the three structural forces behind it and five moves that still work.
- [50/30/20 vs Zero-Based Budgeting](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-budget-methods): Where each method breaks, and the savings-rate ladder (each 5 points = ~$500k over 30 years) that matters more than the method.
- [Lump Sum vs Dollar-Cost Averaging](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-lump-sum-vs-dca): 155 years of S&P 500 data, every starting month — lump sum wins 77% since 1950; DCA-12 costs ~5% expected; 3-month schedules cost under 1%.
- [Rent vs Buy: The Break-Even Math](https://blog.ggaag.com/posts/finance-rent-vs-buy): Full model of a $400k home vs renting and investing the difference; buying wins when appreciation beats investment return by ~2.6%/yr.
